full_judgment:
AFM Abdur Rahman J : Bhaskar Chakraborty, the, accused petitioner, in Tejgaon Police Station Case No. 67 dated 20-9-2000, initiated under sections 406/420 of the Penal Code comprised in GR Case No. 3452 of 2000, pending before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, obtained this Rule under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, on 18-2-2001, challenging the legality and propriety of the entire proceeding, as aforesaid, and the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, has been called upon to show cause as to why the said proceeding should not be quashed. At the time of issuance of the Rule, the proceeding in aforesaid GR Case No. 3452 of 2000 has been stayed by this Court. 

 3. The informant, KMM Iqbal, being the Law Officer of Lever Brothers Bangladesh Limited, lodged Tejgaon Police Station Case No. 67 on 20-9-2000, against the accused petitioner,under sections 406/420 of the Penal Code, alleging, inter alia, that the accused petitioner, Bhaskar Chakraborty, being the owner of a business concern named Alternative Market Research Group has been appointed for inventing Alternative Market for the product of the informant's company and to make the product available door to door of the consumers and, as such, the accused petitioner was allowed under written contract to act as Commission Agent in the year 1998. The accused petitioner, accordingly, was given the product of the Lever Brothers on credit for an amount of Taka 21,89,53600 out of which a balance amount of Taka 16,72,30140 has been left with the accused petitioner, which he did not pay to the company, Lever Brothers Bangladesh Ltd. As such, he committed offence of criminal breach of trust and cheating by way of misappropriating the money as agent of the Lever Brothers Bangladesh Ltd. 

 4. Police commenced investigation and after conclusion of the same, submitted charge sheet against the accused petitioner under sections 406/420 of the Penal Code and also arrested the accused petitioner. The accused petitioner, after preferring a miscellaneous application before the High Court Division, being Criminal Miscellaneous No. 6681 of 2000, under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, obtained ad interim bail on 13-11-2000. Thereafter, challenging the entire proceeding in GR Case No. 3452 of 2000, the accused petitioner preferred this miscellaneous application and obtained the Rule. 

 5. Upon hearing the learned Assistant Attorney-General, Mr AKM Nurul Alam, who appeared on behalf of the State pursuant to the Rule and the learned Advocate, Ms Shakila Rowshan, who obtained the Rule on behalf of the accused petitioner and also the learned Advocate, Mr Md Abdun Noor, appearing on behalf of the informant opposite party No.1 and perusing the FIR and all other materials on record, it appears that the accused petitioner relied upon the principle that the alleged transaction being the business transaction is immune from the allegation of criminal breach of trust and cheating as enunciated by the decision of the case of Dewan Obaidur Rahman vs State and another reported in 1999 BLD (AD) 128, whereas, on the other hand, the State relied upon the ground that the accused petitioner being admittedly agent under the informant company, Lever Brothers Bangladesh Limited, cannot rely upon the principle as laid down in the said case which has distinguishing feature, apparent on the facts of the case. 

 6. The pertinent question as has been raised in this proceeding is, that whether the accused petitioner is involved in a business transaction with the Lever Brothers Bangladesh Ltd to get the benefit of the principle as enunciated in the case of Dewan Obaidur Rahman vs State reported in 1999 BLD (AD) 128 = 4 BLC (AD) 167. 

 7. We have perused the aforesaid judgment involved in the case of Dewan Obaidur Rahman vs State reported in 1999 BLD (AD) 128 = 4 BLC (AD) 167 in which relevant facts involved stated in paragraph No.2 of the Judgment which are as follows: 

 9. In the aforesaid case, the informant complainant, being a seller of certain building materials namely steel window, grill, verandah grill, ventilator, etc. sold those materials to the -accused petitioner as a customer and, as such, the transaction, no doubt a monetary transaction, involved between a seller arid his customer is a business transaction and, as such, the said business transaction, as their Lord-ships in the Appellate Division held, cannot come within the mischief of Sections 405 and 415 of the Penal Code, so as to treat the same transaction as a commission of offence of criminal breach of trust and cheating punishable under sections 406/420 of the Penal Code respectively. But the case is otherwise here, since admittedly the accused petitioner, being the owner of a business concern named Alter native Market Research Group, has been appointed as a Commission Agent of the Lever Brothers Bangladesh Limited. The term Agent has got its own definition as prevailing in the business arena and also as defined in section 182 of the Contract Act, 1872, which runs as follows: 

 12. Admittedly, the accused petitioner, being a Commission Agent, misappropriated the money of his principal Lever Brothers Bangladesh Limited, as alleged in the FIR, the decision given in the case of Dewan Obaidur Rahman vs State reported in 1999 BLD (AD) 128 = 4 BLC (AD) 167, has no manner of application in this case, as it has been corrimitted by the agent not arising out of business transaction as decided by their Lordships in that case.
